doc.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Old friendships with Milt Jackson and Joe Williams
summary: Levy recalls an early Philadelphia gig with Milt Jackson and Tal Farlow, and Joe Williams working as a Regal Theater doorman.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I think they’re just real good friends. We’ve known each other for years. In fact one of the first playing engagements of Milt Hinton, uh, Milt Jackson, was in Philadelphia. He and I and Tal Farlow worked in Philadelphia. That was one of the first playing gigs for Milt, you know, and so that’s how far back we go. We go back quite a way. And we were talking about that the other day, and I said, yeah, we go way, way back. And Joe I remember being a doorman at the Regal Theater and I used to go back stage and he worked part time as a doorman and then he would go and sing at night in a night club, you know. Well he has, I’m sure when you talk to him he had some great experiences to tell you.
I know. It was very hard to stop after an hour. We’ll do part two and three and four.
